Transaction costs of 10 bps each way penalize large rotations; the 35% max position limit and no leverage constrain any defensive repositioning.

NVDA.notes: Sharp 30d pullback of -14.5% below SMA-20/50 at 41% annualized vol, RSI 41.8 not yet oversold; still above SMA-200 and 12-1 momentum (+52.3%) tops the universe. Short-term downtrend inside a larger uptrend - momentum-crash risk versus mean-reversion setup.

META.notes: 90d -12.2% with price below SMA-50/200 despite a sharp recent bounce back above SMA-20 (RSI 61.3); 42% vol. Medium-term trend is broken even though 12-1 momentum (+33.4%) remains high - conflicting signals.

JPM.notes: Steady uptrend above SMA-20/50/200 and within 2.3% of 52-week highs; 30d +2.5% outperformed SPY's -0.6%. Neutral RSI 49.4 and normal vol - low-drama compounder.

XOM.notes: Flat 30d (+0.4%), marginally below SMA-20 but above SMA-50/200; 12-1 momentum slightly negative (-0.2%). No momentum edge versus SPY.

TLT.notes: Mild uptrend above SMA-20/200 with 90d +5.3% roughly in line with SPY; lowest vol in the universe (7.8%) and neutral RSI 57.3. Useful low-volatility diversifier.

GLD.notes: Strongest momentum across all horizons (30d +6.9%, 90d +22.0%, 12-1 +49.7%), well above rising SMAs. RSI at 70 is overbought and 29% vol is elevated - chase risk after a big run.

SPY.notes: Benchmark consolidating within 0.6% of 52-week highs: 30d flat but 90d +6.2% and above all SMAs; RSI 58 with low 13.8% vol. Uptrend intact but leadership is narrowing.

forecaster.method_notes: Drift-based statistical forecasts over the 22-trading-day horizon (2025-11-28 to ~2025-12-31), using only price history up to the decision date; no news, fundamentals, or post-decision information. Key limitations: (1) the method extrapolates recent drift and volatility, so it will lag regime changes and mean reversals; (2) intervals are wide for high-vol names (NVDA p10/p90 spans roughly -16% to +23%, META -12% to +17%), and that width is uncertainty, not evidence to avoid the asset; (3) in-window catalysts such as earnings, Fed meetings, and macro releases are not modeled, which is a particular tail-risk for single-name tech holdings; (4) GLD's strong expected return rests on continued momentum with RSI already at 70, so some fade risk is plausible; (5) point estimates are modest relative to interval widths, so ranking by expected return alone is noisy and should be combined with position limits and transaction costs (10 bps each way).
